title: Arithmetic operators
recap: C++ provides unary plus and minus and the binary addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division operators. Unary minus produces the negation of its operand; it does not modify a named operand by itself.
Integer division discards any fractional part. If a fractional result is required, at least one operand must be floating-point, which can be made explicit with static_cast<double>.
objectives: Combine addition, subtraction, and multiplication in a practical calculation.
Compare integer division with floating-point division.
Use static_cast<double> to request a fractional quotient.
Apply unary minus to reverse a signed adjustment.
warnings: Dividing two int values performs integer division even when the result initializes a double.
Do not use a final numeric literal in place of the arithmetic expression.
This exercise does not need input or formatted decimal output.
challenge: Produce a session report from 155 total minutes split among 4 sessions. Calculate whole minutes per session with integer division and exact minutes per session by converting totalMinutes to double before division. Separately calculate a 3-point net score from five 2-point gains and a 7-point penalty, then negate that score to show unary minus.
hints: totalMinutes / sessions uses integer division because both operands are int.
Use static_cast<double>(totalMinutes) / sessions for the exact quotient.
Calculate netScore as gains * pointsPerGain - penalty, then initialize reversedScore with -netScore.
